Daily Quiz.question: ১) Who wrote the first English Comedy?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Nicholas Udall is the Writer of first English Comedy.
Nicholas Udall is a writer from Elizabethan age.
He wrote 'Ralph Roister Doister (1553)' which is the first English Comedy.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) The character 'Yahoo' is found in -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The character 'Yahoo' is found in - Gulliver’s Travels (fiction).

Gulliver’s Travels, original title 'Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World', four-part satirical work by Anglo-Irish author Jonathan Swift, published anonymously in 1726 as Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.

Its important characters are:
- Gulliver,
- Blefuscudian,
- Yahoos,
- Houyhnhnms,
- Lilliputians,
- Laputans.
Houyhnhnms in Gulliver’s Travels are horses.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) ''To err is human; to forgive, divine'' is quoted by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
'To err is human; to forgive, divine.' is quoted by Alexandar Pope, from his An essay on criticism

Alexander Pope is a Mock Heroic Poet.
His famous quotations:
- Charms strike the sight but merit strikes the heart.
- A little learning is a dangerous thing.
- To err is human, to forgive is divine.
- An honest man is the noblest work of God.
- The proper study of mankind is man.
- Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.
- Hope springs eternal in the human breast.

Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Which of the following book is known as embryo of English novel?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Arcadia – a book that bears the embryo of the English novel.
(The Countess of Pembroke's Arcadia)
- It was Written by Sir Philip Sidney.
- It was published in 1590. 

Sir Philip Sidney (1554 - 1586) was one of the most prominent poets of the Elizabethan era.
His famous works:
- Astrophel and Stella,
- The Lady of May
- An Apology for Poetry.

Source: An ABC OF English Literature - Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman and Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Richardson's "Pamela" is an example of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Pamela, in full Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded, novel in epistolary style by Samuel Richardson, published in 1740 and based on a story about a servant and the man who, failing to seduce her, marries her.

Epistolary Novel 
- A novel told through in the form of letters.
- The narrative of this type of novel is carried forward by letters written by one or more of the characters of that novel.

Samuel Richardson (1689 - 1761), an English novelist. 
His major novels were:
- Pamela (1740) and
- Clarissa (1747–48).

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) William Congreve belongs to -
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Congreve is a writer from The Restoration Period.

His notable works are:
- The Double Dealer
- Love for Love
- The Way of The World.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Satiric poem ‘Hudibras’ is written by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
'Hudibras' is a satiric poem Written by Samuel Butler. 
- It Was published in several parts beginning in 1663. 

Samuel Butler was an English novelist and critic.
- He is the writer of the Restoration Period.
- His famous satire in verse is Hudibras.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Which literary work is not belongs to Jonathan Swift?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Jonathan Swift is the greatest satirist of the 18th century.
He belongs to the Neoclassical Period of English Literature.

His famous novels:
- Gulliver's Travels,
- A tale of a Tub,
- A Modest Proposal,
- A Journey to Stella,
- The Battle of the Books.

- 'Robinson Crusoe' is a Novel written by Daniel Defoe. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) The Pilgrim’s Progress is a religious _____.
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Pilgrim’s Progress is a religious allegory.
- It was written by the English writer John Bunyan.
- It published in two parts in 1678 and 1684.
- The work is a symbolic vision of the good man’s pilgrimage through life. 

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Which one is written by Caedmon?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Caedmon is the first known poet or earliest epic poet of English literature.
- He is also called Father of English Sacred Song.
- He is the writer of Paraphrase.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) The character 'Friday' is taken from-
Daily Quiz.exp:
• 'Robinson Crusoe' first published in London in 1719.
- Defoe’s first long work of fiction, it introduced two of the most-enduring characters in English literature: Robinson Crusoe and Friday.

• Daniel Defoe is a famous English writer, journalist, pamphleteer and spy.
• He is famous for his novels.
His novels are:
- Robinson Crusoe,
- Captain Singleton,
- Moll Flanders,
- Colonel Jack,
- Roxana: The Fortunate Mistress.


Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica and Robinson Crusoe.

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) On the death of Edward king John Milton wrote-
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Milton wrote Lycidas (Pastoral elegy) on death of Edward king.
Edward king was friend of John Milton.

- Paradise lost is an epic written by John Milton.
- He is called great master of Blank Verse.
- He also wrote:
     - L'Allegro
     - Paradise regained
     - Of Education

Source: An ABC OF English Literature - Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman and Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) ‘Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.'  Who uttered this line?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Some of the quotes of Alexander Pope from An Essay on Criticism are-
- 'Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.'
- 'To err is human, to forgive, divine.'
- 'An honest man's the noblest work of God.'
 
Alexander Pope is called Mock Heroic Poet.
Famous epics of Alexander Pope is 'The Rape of the Lock'.
His famous works are-
- An Essay on Criticism,
- The Dunciad,
- The Imitation of Horace,
- An Essay on Man,
- Letter to Gay.

Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) ‘Captain Hercules Vinegar’ is the pen name of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
• Captain Hercules Vinegar’ is the pen name of Henry Fielding.
• Henry Fielding regarded as the 'Father of Modern English Novel'.
• He is famous for Picaresque Novel.
• His pen name is Captain Hercules Vinegar.

• His famous plays:
- Rape Upon Rape,
- The Temple Beau,
- The Tragedy of Tragedies,
- The Modern Husband etc.

• His famous Novels:
- Tom Jones,
- Amelia,
- Joseph Andrews etc.

Source: Encyclopedia Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Who supervised the compilation of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Alfred the Great encouraged and supervised the compilation of the earliest English Prose Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

Alfred the Great (born 849 - died 899) who reigned over England from 871 to 901. 
- He prevented England from falling to the Danes and promoted learning and literacy.
- Compilation of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle began during his reign, circa 890.
- Alfred considered learning and literacy to be crucial for the acquisition of wisdom and therefore necessary for men to live in accordance with God’s will.
- He is called founder of English prose.

Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) Among them who is known as Political Philosopher?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679) is a political philosopher.
- He belongs to Commonwealth Period of English literature.
- His famous book is Leviathan (1651).

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) English philosopher Roger Bacon is known as _______.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Roger Bacon, byname Doctor Mirabilis (Latin: “Wonderful Teacher”), (born c. 1220, Gloucester, England — died 1292 in Oxford),
- An English Franciscan philosopher and educational reformer who was a major medieval proponent of experimental science.
- Bacon studied mathematics, astronomy, optics, alchemy, and languages.
- He was the first European to describe in detail the process of making gunpowder, and he proposed flying machines and motorized ships and carriages.

Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) “An Essay Concerning Human Understanding” - a literary work of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Locke (born August 29, 1632 - died October 28) is an English philosopher whose works lie at the foundation of modern philosophical empiricism and political liberalism. 
- He was an inspirer of both the European Enlightenment and the Constitution of the United States.
- John Locke’s most famous works are- 
- An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689), in which he developed his theory of ideas and his account of the origins of human knowledge in experience. and
- Two Treatises of Government. 

Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) ‘Iliad’ is translated into English by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
George Chapman, (born 1559, Hitchin, Hertfordshire, Eng.—died May 12, 1634, London), English poet and dramatist, whose translation of Homer long remained the standard English version.
- George Chapman translated Homer’s 'Iliad' and 'Odyssey' into English.
- The first books of his translation of the 'Iliad' appeared in 1598. It was completed in 1611, and his version of the Odyssey appeared in 1616. Chapman’s Homer contains passages of great power and beauty and inspired the sonnet of John Keats “On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer” (1815).

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) The literary criticism ‘Preface to Shakespeare’ was written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
The literary criticism ‘Preface to Shakespeare’ was written by Samuel Johnson.
- Samuel Johnson who said in his 'Preface to Shakespeare' (1765) that “there is always an appeal open from criticism to nature.
- It has long been considered a classic document of English literary criticism.
- He was a famous critic of Shakespeare.

Dr. Samuel Johnson is a writer from The Age of Sensibility (1745-1798).
Dr. Samuel Johnson's major works:
- Dictionary (1755),
- The History of Rasselas, Prince of Abyssinia (1759),
- Preface to Shakespeare (1765).

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.
